title: Quirós and Torres: Espíritu Santo and the Torres Strait, 1605–07
summary: Quirós led three Spanish ships out of Callao to find the great southern continent. He found the largest island of Vanuatu, named it Austrialia del Espíritu Santo and tried to found a city there; within five weeks he left, and the ships parted. Quirós went home to New Spain; Torres opened his orders and sailed on, through the strait between New Guinea and Australia that bears his name, to Manila. Torres's road beyond the strait is not drawn.

events.label: Big Bay: La Nueva Jerusalén
events.text: Quirós took the island for Spain, laid out a city and a church, and named the bay for the River Jordan. The Spanish stayed about five weeks. Ni-Vanuatu people lived all round the bay; the account is Spanish, and the Spanish record of the people they met is thin.

events.label: Torres Strait
events.text: Torres sailed through the strait between New Guinea and Australia. His report stayed in Spanish archives until the British took Manila in 1762; Alexander Dalrymple named the strait for him in 1769.
